import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_94/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_94/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_94/training_2.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)  # Source3_94_0
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)  # Source3_94_1
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)  # Source3_94_2

# Step 1: JOIN Source3_94_0 and Source3_94_1 on "movie_id"
# This join is between df0 and df1 on 'movie_id'
df_join_0_1 = pd.merge(df0, df1, on="movie_id", how="inner", suffixes=('_0', '_1'))

# Step 2: JOIN the above result with Source3_94_2 on "user_id"
# Note: df2 has 'user_id', df_join_0_1 has 'user_id' from Source3_94_1 (renamed to user_id)
# Actually, df_join_0_1 has 'user_id' from Source3_94_1 (no suffix added to user_id)
df_join_all = pd.merge(df_join_0_1, df2, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Step 3: Group by Source3_94_0.movie_id and Source3_94_0.title
# Columns from Source3_94_0 kept as is: movie_id, title
# Aggregations:
#   F = avg(rating where sex == 'F')
#   M = avg(rating where sex == 'M')

# Create columns for conditional ratings
df_join_all['rating_F'] = np.where(df_join_all['sex'] == 'F', df_join_all['rating'], np.nan)
df_join_all['rating_M'] = np.where(df_join_all['sex'] == 'M', df_join_all['rating'], np.nan)

# Group by movie_id and title (from Source3_94_0)
grouped = df_join_all.groupby(['movie_id', 'title'], as_index=False).agg({
    'rating_F': 'mean',
    'rating_M': 'mean'
})

# Rename columns to match target schema
grouped.rename(columns={'rating_F': 'F', 'rating_M': 'M'}, inplace=True)

# Ensure correct dtypes as per target schema
grouped['movie_id'] = grouped['movie_id'].astype(int)
grouped['title'] = grouped['title'].astype(str)
grouped['F'] = grouped['F'].astype(float)
grouped['M'] = grouped['M'].astype(float)

# Save the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_94/target_multisource.csv"
grouped.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Read source files with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_94/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_94/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_94/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source3_94_1 and Source3_94_2 on user_id
joined_1_2 = pd.merge(source1, source2, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Join Source3_94_0 and the above join on movie_id
joined_all = pd.merge(source0, joined_1_2, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Create columns for ratings by sex
# Use np.where to assign rating if sex matches, else NaN
joined_all["rating_F"] = np.where(joined_all["sex"] == "F", joined_all["rating"], np.nan)
joined_all["rating_M"] = np.where(joined_all["sex"] == "M", joined_all["rating"], np.nan)

# Group by movie_id and title, aggregate average rating for F and M
result = joined_all.groupby(["movie_id", "title"], as_index=False).agg(
    F = ("rating_F", "mean"),
    M = ("rating_M", "mean")
)

# Write output with exact target schema and column names
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_94/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
